subject: Temporary reservation / autoscale exception request for QuantaCorp batch pilot
messages:
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, eileen@quantacorp.com
Cc: ops@quantacorp.com
Date: 2028-03-30T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary reserved slices for QuantaCorp batch pilot (Mar 30 - Apr 6)

Hi team,

QuantaCorp (cc'd) is starting a week-long pilot tonight that will run large nightly batch reranks and embedding jobs between 02:00-06:00 UTC. The pilot is expected to spike token throughput and will likely trigger our autoscaler repeatedly — the customer is sensitive to tail latency and wants predictable 95th pct response during the pilot window.

Ask: can we provision a temporary dedicated carveout (1 x p4d-equivalent slice, 24/7) for the pilot window (2028-03-30 to 2028-04-06) or alternatively approve an autoscale policy exception that allows burst capacity without evicting other pilots? I attached the pilot resource plan and last-night capacity snapshot.

Key numbers from QuantaCorp: expected nightly peak 18k tokens/sec aggregated, typical sequence length ~1.2k, burst duration 3-4 hours. They will run ~20 concurrent jobs at peak.

If a hard reservation isn't possible, we need a mitigation plan (quantized model variant, rate limiter, or strict time-window gating) and a clear rollback/fallback if SLOs degrade. This pilot is tied to an active negotiation (deal D-9832) so we need an ops decision by EOD today to confirm commercial terms.

Attachments: pilot_resource_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), capacity_snapshot-20280329.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
From: dev.patel@redwood.com
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: eileen@quantacorp.com, ops@quantacorp.com
Date: 2028-03-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserved slices for QuantaCorp batch pilot (Mar 30 - Apr 6)

Thanks Jasmine — quick clarifying Qs before I commit to provisioning:
- Is the 18k tokens/sec estimate sustained across the 3-4 hour window or does it concentrate into sub-minute bursts?
- Can QuantaCorp stagger job starts to smooth the peak (they said yes in principle but need confirmation)?
- Are we able to run them on a quantized 4-bit variant for the pilot? That would reduce GPU memory and pressure.

Operational options I see:
1) Temporary hard slice (24/7) for the week — highest predictability, but we need approval for carving out from shared pool; cost charged to the pilot.
2) Autoscale exception: raise burst cap for that tenant for the nightly window; less isolation but faster to enable.
3) Workload-level throttling + prefetched KV caches to reduce peak tokens.

If they can confirm 18k is an aggregate with short microbursts we could probably do option 2 + throttling. If it’s sustained, option 1 is safer.

I can spin up the slice but will need infra signoff (Marcus) and a ticket; I'll add INFRA-2145 as the change request.

--
Dev Patel
Capacity Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, eileen@quantacorp.com, ops@quantacorp.com
Date: 2028-03-30T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserved slices for QuantaCorp batch pilot (Mar 30 - Apr 6)

Adding product context — QuantaCorp is a strategic pilot tied to a VP-level approval; we promised predictable latency for the pilot. They cannot easily stagger jobs due to their internal ETL windows. They're willing to pay for a short reservation if that simplifies ops.

From a commercial perspective: if we can offer an explicit reserved lane for Apr pilot nights we should do it — it removes risk in negotiation. Please include expected cost impact in the ticket so Sales can confirm charges.

If infra needs constraints: we can accept a 1-week hard reservation limited to the pilot night window (02:00-06:00 UTC) rather than 24/7; that reduces pressure on daytime shared workloads. But priority is guaranteed tail latency during the defined window.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: eileen@quantacorp.com, ops@quantacorp.com
Date: 2028-03-30T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserved slices for QuantaCorp batch pilot (Mar 30 - Apr 6)

We can provision a temporary carveout for the nightly window only (02:00-06:00 UTC) for the pilot week. Notes / caveats:
- We'll implement a time-windowed reservation that reserves capacity during the 4-hr nightly window and releases slices during the day. This minimizes daytime disruption.
- We need an INFRA change (INFRA-2145) and a rollback plan; will require on-call awareness for the first two nights.
- Recommend pairing the reservation with a 4-bit quantized model variant for the pilot requests — that will reduce GPU footprint ~35% and lower cost.
- There is potential impact to other low-priority pilots during the nightly window; we should notify stakeholders of the transient availability change.

If Product signs off on the time-windowed reservation approach I will schedule the change to deploy tonight at 01:30 UTC and monitor. Marcus will lead the deployment and follow up with metrics.

Attachments referenced: capacity_snapshot-20280329.pdf (shared in Jasmine's initial email).

Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Compute & Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: eileen@quantacorp.com, ops@quantacorp.com
Date: 2028-03-30T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserved slices for QuantaCorp batch pilot (Mar 30 - Apr 6)

Thanks all — summary and next steps:

Decision: time-windowed nightly reservation approved for pilot week (02:00-06:00 UTC, 2028-03-30 through 2028-04-06). Marcus to schedule change INFRA-2145 tonight at 01:30 UTC.

Mitigations: run quantized model variant where feasible (Dev to validate compatibility), Sales will bill pilot per agreed rates (Kim to confirm cost). On-call will watch first two nights and we’ll roll back if we see eviction/quality regressions.

Action items:
- Marcus: deploy reservation (INFRA-2145), confirm completion and post initial metrics in this thread.
- Dev: verify quantized variant viability and add fallback to standard model if inference quality drops.
- Kim: confirm commercial terms with Sales and send invoice language to QuantaCorp.
- Jasmine: notify QuantaCorp (cc'd) of the plan and the monitoring cadence.

QuantaCorp — please confirm you accept the nightly window plan and cost model so we can proceed.
